title: ioctl_key_export_private leaks private key bytes on copy_to_user failure
description: ioctl_key_export_private() installs the private key bytes into state->outbuf and then calls copy_to_user to return the keylen in the op struct. If copy_to_user fails (ret = -EFAULT), the function returns -EFAULT to userspace. The private key bytes remain in state->outbuf (state->outbuf_drained == 0, state->outbuf_len == outlen). A subsequent read() on the KEY fd will then return those private key bytes to userspace even though the copy_to_user for the keylen field failed. This is probably the intended behavior (the bytes are still available), but represents a correctness issue: the caller got -EFAULT from KEY_EXPORT_PRIVATE, does not know outlen, and may not know to read(). More importantly: state->outbuf now holds private key material indefinitely until the fd is closed or another KEY_EXPORT_PRIVATE call replaces it. If the process forks after this, the child fd inherits the buffered private key. This is a key material exposure risk. The existing outbuf_drained/outbuf_len tracking means the bytes persist across reads until drained. Trigger: KEY_GENERATE → KEY_EXPORT_PRIVATE with bad uarg pointer → -EFAULT → private key bytes sit in outbuf → read() drains them without caller being aware of the export.
